newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand stops baht-raising in bourse - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Thailand stops baht-raising in bourse - brokers.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Tuesday informally told local brokerages not to handle big lot stocks transactions with foreigners in its latest move to stop offshore players from raising baht through the bourse, brokers said.

"There were a number of big lot sales by foreigners yesterday as their new way to get the baht. So the central bank today asked all brokerage firms not to make big-lot transactions with foreigners," said one broker at a local house.
Senior central bank officials were not available for comment on the talk and stock exchange officials said they had not heard of any such move so far.
The talk caused the Thai stock index to plunge at the open by over 2.0 percent. At 0430 GMT, the index was steadier at 532.98 or a 0.28 percent loss.

Brokers said some foreign players, in need of baht to cover their short positions after last month's speculative attack on the currency, were raising the much-needed Thai unit through the bourse after other local supply sources were cut by the central bank from mid-May.

After the speculative attack on the baht, the central bank, in an attempt to punish speculators, told local financial institutions not to sell baht to offshore players except for trade and direct investment purposes.

This caused a two-tier baht market to develop, one offshore and the other onshore. It also forced a scramble for baht among foreign players anxious to cover their positions and sent the currency to a 13-year high last week.
An analyst at a local brokerage said the central bank wanted any stocks transaction made with foreigners in the local bourse would have to be settled in U.S. dollars.
The move was to ensure that the baht did not change hands to foreigners as they conducted stocks transactions in the local market, he added.
